I am a little bit disappointed cause it’s under construction when I visit it.. But it’s still worth it

First time here. It is a peaceful an interesting place to go and explore and, of course, visit a shrine. It is steep, so be careful. Also, be aware of the routes from place to place. It is not so big, but can be confusing.

Narrow street with food places. Very nice! On Friday evening was a bit hard to get a seat so I recommend going earlier
Amazing alleyway, lots of food and amazing people.

Amazing place just before heading to Wilson Prom. Service with smiles, firewood pizza oven, Deli with a lot of Italian products (fresh pasta,wines and much more). Fabulous atmosphere even on a rainy day. A bite of Puglia in the Prom! Definitely need to stop here!

Amazing veggie pizza and delicious focaccia, one of the best pizza we’ve had in Australia ! They also had french chips (Brets - the beat chips’ brand ever imo) and it was so cool and surprising to see that brand in Meenyian!! We finished our meal next to the fire with a delicious ice cream !

Some reviews mention there can be many stairs, which can be challenging to climb.
1983.edj: この神社を訪れたユーザーのクチコミでは、静かで落ち着いた雰囲気や、アズマシャクナゲのような美しい季節の花々、そして温泉街の素晴らしい眺めが高く評価されています。また、社務所が閉まっている際には近くの飲食店で御朱印がもらえることや、手入れの行き届いた境内も特徴です。 クチコミの中には、階段が多く、上るのが大変だという声もあります。

rv.t: Here no need entrance fee. Have to climb up the stairs to reach the shrine. It is a small shrine.

Beautiful shine a bit uphill and off the way from the town center. However, it was on route from my accommodation to the town center. It has the most beautiful cleansing booth i have seen in a long while. Very colorful and flower filled

Very unique Shinto shrine in the heart of kusatsu onsens. A pleasant must visit site. Enjoy the scenic beauty and pleasant weather. You can get a good view of the onsens without the smell. So a must visit for at least that reason. The temple is really old and well preserved. A must visit

1984.a: Kōsenji Temple, 甲446 Kusatsu, Agatsuma District, Gunma 377-1711, Japan

1984.edj: 石段の上にある寺院。冬の雪景色と湯けむり上る温泉の景色が有名。

rv.t: I visited last December, and there was a bit of snow, which added to the charm of the place. It’s a lovely little temple that you’ll pass by when walking around Kusatsu. If you get the chance, I also recommend staying overnight, the atmosphere is quite different.

Here you no need to pay entrance fee. Is a small buddhist temple. There is a stairs to climb near Yubatake. Climbing up you can see the view of Yubatake. Up the buddhist temple you can see a beautiful five-story pagoda. At night you can see the light of the five-story pagoda from Yubatake.
A scenic spot looking down on the town. In the month of February, care needed when descending the icy steps.

1985.a: Shirahata Hot Spring, 417-1 Kusatsu, Agatsuma District, Gunma 377-1711, Japan
1985.aj: 〒377-1711 群馬県吾妻郡草津町草津４１７−１ 白旗乃湯（白旗源泉共同浴場）

rv.t: This a traditional free public bath. Definitely go here if you want the real local experience. Take your shoes off right at the entrance then the “changing room” is right there next to the bath (it’s just an area with a wooden shelf to leave your clothes). The place is very small but the local people are very friendly. This was my first onsen, they show me how to use it. The water is super hot (I think around 50…
Free public bath. I went on a weekday night and it wasn't crowded at all. The hot spring water is really hot, but worth trying to soak in, especially in winter.

I’ve been to 4 free sentos and this one is the second hottest. I could only soak my legs in at the beginning but after a while I could do my whole body as long as not too close to water source. Second visit at 630am, the smaller pool was 80% full and the bigger one was only 30%.

rv.t: 夏は水陸両用バス冬は観光船の乗船口です。 湖の直ぐ近くで橋が上に見られ景色は最高❗️ 建物の裏に遊具が少しありますので子どもも楽しめます。 駐車場出口付近の左手に展望台の登り口が有ります。登って見たらあずまやがあったのでお弁当を持ってハイキング気分で登るのも良いと思います🎵結構キツイ坂です❗️
あまり知られていないのか、とても空いていました。去年の11月にオープンしたみたいです。 建物が入りづらい(°▽°) 水陸両用バス！面白そう！ 店内の食事はリーズナブル。 揚げたてポテト200円。 JAF会員は烏龍茶S無料。これはうれしい！
訪問した時は 雨だったので ちょっとゆっくり出来なかったのですが 庭とか 綺麗に公園のようになってました。 建物内で御城印 購入しました。

This was a really cute store. I wanted to try the letterpress printing workshop but they were sold out for the day. Next time I’m in Onomichi I’ll book in advance.
尾道で活版印刷体験が出来る珍しいお店。 今回は時間がなかったので、体験は出来なかったですが、店内にはポストカードなどグッズが置いてあったので、入店させていただきました☺️ 尾道を感じるポストカード、ポチ袋やメッセージカードなどがあり、プレゼントやお土産にも◯ 活版印刷体験は予約が必要です。 目の前には線路があり電車が通るので、尾道らしい雰囲気も楽しめます🚃

1989.edj: 丘の上に建つ寺院群。カラフルで複雑な装飾が施され、多くの仏像が安置されている。

rv.t: The temple is truly one of the most breathtaking landmarks in Penang and a must visit destination for anyone exploring the island. As one of the largest and most important Buddhist temples in Southeast Asia, it offers a remarkable blend of spirituality, culture, history, and stunning architecture.From the moment you enter the temple complex, you are greeted by beautifully decorated prayer halls, intricate carvings…

One of the most famous spots in Penang. It has been renovated extensively, with many new buildings added since I was young. The temple's signature feature is the massive Guan Yin statue, which is roughly 30 meters tall. ​In addition to the main statue, there are many other deities and intricate carvings inside the temple, and it takes quite a while to explore them all. Even though I was just roaming around and…

Kek Lok Si Temple is one of Penang’s most impressive cultural attractions and an experience that should not be rushed. The temple complex is much larger than we expected, with beautifully detailed architecture, colourful prayer halls, landscaped gardens, statues and peaceful spaces to explore. Every level revealed something different, and the elevated location provided impressive views across Air Itam and George…

rv.t: Beautiful cafe tucked in Nishihara neighbourhood, the inside is filled with natural sunlight and the terrace is surrounded by a large tree / greenery. Very peaceful and serene. I was lucky because I only had to wait 10 minutes and the cafe was not super crowded on a weekday around noon time. Coffee was good and the sweet pastry (citron cake) was delicious too. Service was attentive and friendly. The vibes are giving…

Such a lovely atmosphere! Dropped in here for a coffee to escape the rain and had a dirty chai with oat milk. The interior is gorgeous, such a calm atmosphere. And excellent coffee 🫶🏼 They also offer gluten free granola ✨
Hidden gem, lovely building with outdoor seatings. The hot latte was good, iced latte was average. Everyone seems to be eating the hotdog but it takes about 20min to get one.

rv.t: Classic HK play experience. Lots of memories here. Strong supporter, however there aren't enough places to sit or lounge that is away from the sun. Unfortunately, it isn't filled with much to do indoors as well. The displays and animals seem to be decent, but it is starting to show the age a little more now. Looking forward to the next renovation, of a revamped and updated park.

Fantastic day at Ocean Park Hong Kong! The park offers the perfect mix of thrilling rides, amazing animal exhibits, and beautiful ocean views. Everything is clean, well organized, and easy to explore. The cable car and Ocean Express are attractions on their own, with breathtaking scenery. The staff are friendly and helpful, and there are plenty of dining options throughout the park. It’s a great destination for…

Ocean Park Cable Car offers an amazing ride with stunning panoramic views. The highlight is the beautiful sight of Nam Long Mountain, especially on clear days – perfect for photos. Smooth ride, well-maintained cabins, and a great way to enjoy the scenery from above. Definitely worth trying if you visit the area!

rv.t: While visiting Kurashiki, we came across this traditional Japanese restaurant and have it a try. The wait list was quite long. We went across to get a drink while waiting. We ordered wild boar rice bowl and fish rice bowl. Food was healthy, good portion and delicious. I guess this restaurant is at the bottom of a small hotel. But we didn't stay here, we just trying out the restaurant.

I stayed two nights at Yurinan, and old-style house in the Bikan-chiku (traditional buildings) area of the city, just 10 minutes walk from the station. The staff and other guests gave me a very warm welcome. It felt like my home away from home instantly. I shared a room with other Japanese girls, who became my new friends. The futons were very comfortable...and the hot water bottle in my bed was a special treat! I…

Its a long queue but its worth it. I love the unique taste and freshness of the ingredients. The restaurant itself is a piece of art. Make sure to enjoy the happy pudding. Best pudding ever. Love this place. From the atmosphere to the food.

rv.t: This is the largest waterfall by volume in all of Southeast Asia! The entire Mekong river has to go through here. There are multiple viewpoints here which let you see the various falls and rapids from different angles. I highly recommend visiting this place. It is a must-do when you visit Don Det.

An amazing waterfall, surrounded by cute paths, interesting flowers and a small temple dedicated to a sacred tree. Definitely worth the visit just for the vibes but also because it's the "largest waterfall by volume in Asia", so that's fun

Stunning place that's also fascinating. I'd definitely visit again. The waterfall is gushing so much and it's even more intriguing that it's the most powerful one in the world when it comes to water flow. In fact, it's more than all of the other top 10 combined. Mind blowing! The toilets come with a small charge but it's fine. They're not the most clean but they're not horrific as well, especially for public toilet…

1995.edj: 古代ヒンドゥー教寺院の遺跡。後に仏教寺院に改修された。高台にあり、眼下には素晴らしい景色が広がる。

rv.t: A very beautiful and peaceful place. Wat Phou is an amazing old temple with a long history which I visited a long time ago. I love the old stone buildings and the green mountains behind them. It is a bit of a long walk up the stairs, but the view from the top is great! It is best to go early in the morning when it is not too hot. The light is perfect for taking photos. Definitely a must-see in Champasak!

Large tempel complex area. Part of the old Khmer empire though far away from famous sites like Angkhor Wat. Make your way up the steps to find yourself a beautiful view of the area. Looking down you'll have a better understanding of the site' size. The buildings are covered with inscriptions, figures and animals carvings. Walk behind the top temple and you can find massive boulders and a water source.

A beautiful temple well worth visiting and less than an hour from Pakse. Reasonably priced to get in. Fantastic views from the top. It is a long walk but well worth it. It was very quiet with only a few other visitors which made the experience all the better.

rv.t: Wat Sisaket has such a calm, memorable feel to it. I liked how the old pagoda is surrounded by flowers and big trees, which makes the whole visit feel peaceful and shaded. The small seating area at the back was a nice touch too, giving me a quiet spot to sit down and take a break before continuing on.

When Siam leveled Vientiane in 1827, virtually every temple in the city was burned to the ground. Every temple, except Wat Si Saket. The plot twist? An architectural coincidence saved its life. When King Anouvong built Wat Si Saket in 1818, he chose a multi-tiered roof and cloistered courtyard modeled after Siamese style rather than traditional Lao design. When the invading army arrived, the temple felt so familiar…

This temple is combination of a little of museum, cemetery monuments and the buildings where monks lives. 30,000 kips is not much but it doesn’t give museum vibe. If u are the fans for antique, worth a visit but for normal people, not much to look at. Museum is inside one medium room.

rv.t: This was all done on a Sunday and it was not that busy. I would recommend coming during this time. The experience was amazing and is a must do in Vientiane. My favorite was being able to go inside this dungeon type deal that is made up of four floors and climbing up to the top to take panoramic shots of the area. It was absolutely stunning. I mean it feels like Egypt of being able to walk with old statues in this…

While it’s quite a way out of town and a bit of a drive, this park is worth a visit It has a collection of nearly 100 Buddhas in various forms. It’s not huge but is unique. I love that you can go in the ball statue and stand on top, getting a panoramic view of the park. In theory you can climb the tower at the other end, but the stairs are ‘fun’ so I only went up a little way. I spent over an hour wandering around…

It is a bit far from the city but worth a visit if you hv half day extra. I took bus no.14 from Talat Sao Central Bus station, and reach the Buddha park in around 50 mins. The fare was 25,000 kip (hv to pay in cash). There are a lot of Buddha statues inside the park, very interesting.

I also appreciated the kind lady at the entrance who helped me put on a traditional long sinh before entering. It was a thoughtful gesture that made the visit feel more respectful and memorable. The only thing that made me uncomfortable was…

Lovely ti hear about the old history of Laos. The entrance fee is 30000 Kip for foreigners. The story line od this place is painted and kept in the side corridors. The other corridors have the broken statues of the various deities like Buddha. Old ruins that has been restored. Ample parking space.

This is one of the must do tourist attractions in Vientiane. Its worth a visit and takes a couple of hours to do it justice. The main temple hall is massive and really impressive, but no pictures inside. The giant laying Buddha and Stupa. The Stupa seems to be the most iconic part of the site, even though there are lots of other buildings. I love the Starduck coffee. This is one of the must-do sites in Vientiane and…

Whether you visit in the morning…

One of the main attraction in vientiane make sure to visit this place. You can also go up and just pay at the counter . Its a small gate where you can spend maybe 20minutes . Best time to visit sunset where you can see the view from the top.

An interesting claim up the 192 stairs! Keeps you in shape! Very interesting information in the hallways about the construction of the monument and as well about the history of the various tribes and cultures from Lao! It’s a must go if you have the time, as the view is excellent!

Closed to traffic each evening, it operates as a calm, shopping area with a focus on regional crafts and local produce. The primary positive feature is the relaxed environment. Unlike many bustling night markets across Southeast Asia, vendors here do not engage in high-pressure sales…

this is more of an "evening market" since things wrap up by 10 PM. 葛原岡・大仏ハイキングコース 極楽寺の駐輪場にバイクを停め、風情ある街並みを抜けて長谷駅を経由し、まずは銭洗弁財天神社、そして葛原岡神社へと足を運びました。そこからハイキングコースへ入り、木漏れ日が降り注ぐ山道をゆったりと進みます。コース全体の所要時間は約1時間ほど。ほどよい起伏があるものの体への負担は少なく、のびやかな気持ちで歩くことができました。 このコースは、鎌倉の天園や祇園山のハイキングルートと比べても穏やかで、より気軽に自然を楽しめる印象です。森の中へと続く木製の階段は、苔むした木々に囲まれ、どこか神秘的な雰囲気。静寂の中、木々の枝葉を揺らすそよ風や、木立の奥から聞こえる鳥のさえずりが耳に心地よく響きます。道すがら、陽光に照らされた蝶がひらひらと舞い、草の間からは季節の草花が顔をのぞかせていました。 自然の美しさに包まれながらの散策は、心を静め、豊かな時間を与えてくれるものでした。
從openstreetmap看起來，從錢洗弁財天或者佐助稲荷神社都能進入該步道，但事實上我實際走發現根本沒辦法，佐助稻荷有路徑但已經被封閉，錢洗弁財天更是完全找不到，所以若是要進入大佛步道，最快方式似乎就是只能從源氏山公園進入。步道整體來說算親民，落差起伏不大，但落葉太多也滿容易滑，途中有一個廢墟舊野村研究所廢墟，有興趣的人可以去逛逛。

rv.t: This cafe tea shop tucked behind a small street corner from the main busy street of Arashiyama is a bliss escape from the large crowds… only a short distance walk from the train station. It looks like an old Japanese house that is inclosed with a front garden and inside has ample dining space with tables and a tatami mat dining area. This sweet shop offers a variety of hot or cold drinks like coffee, tea, and juices…

A cozy cafe in Arashiyama, Kyoto. It’s a beautifully renovated traditional house with a modern touch, making it a super relaxing space. The lush greenery in the garden was stunning. You can grill your own dango (rice dumplings) and enjoy them with a bowl of matcha. They also offer a breakfast set in the morning. One of the highlights is toasting adorable cat-shaped bread and pairing it with sweet red bean paste or…

Grilling my own dango was the highlight for me at eXcafe Kyoto Arashiyama Main Store. It made the visit feel a little more fun and hands-on than a typical cafe stop. The place does require one item per person, so it’s good to go in expecting that, and there was a queue, but it moved quickly enough that it never felt like a hassle.
